findings.title: Stress gate's per-scenario 2x detection is conditional on the evaluation count
findings.claim: The stress gate's per-scenario detection target is DETECTION_TARGET=2.0, but its 2x arm (the solver-work count, SCENARIO_WORK_FACTOR=1.5) only moves when the regression adds scipy evaluations, and its CPU arm sits at the documented concession SCENARIO_BUDGET_FACTOR=3.0; a measured cost-only regression (wrap optimizer._batch_fd_gradient to run twice, bit-identical objective) raises solve CPU 1.68-1.81x over two takes while solver_evals reads exactly 1.0000 and no check fires.
findings.mechanism: SolverWork sums scipy nfev+njev over optimizer._scoped_minimize. All simulation cost of one L-BFGS iteration is produced inside a single fun/jac call (batched jac _batch_fd_gradient: 96 rows; objective _space_traj: 96 scalar steps), so a slower or repeated kernel adds zero evaluations and leaves the whole iterate path bit-identical. The count is the gate's only machine-portable 2x detector (tests/stress.py's own record: the per-scenario CPU factor 'STAYS AT 3.0' because the solver's basin is bimodal across platforms, and three CPU-denominated candidates were rejected); a cost-only regression is therefore invisible to it, and 1.68-1.81x is under the 3.0x CPU concession.

evidence.unit: ratio (cost-only arm solve_cpu_ms / baseline solve_cpu_ms); second take 1.6832 at load1 51.61
evidence.machine: Apple M1 8 GB, macOS 25.6.0, numpy on OpenBLAS, threads pinned to 1
evidence.contention_note: round-5 fan-out, shared audit box. Two takes: cpu_ratio 1.8071 at load1 111.24 and 1.6832 at load1 51.61 (thread_factor 1.000-1.001 both). The conclusion is load-invariant because 3.0 is the ceiling; the exact ratio is provisional and re-taken quiet.

perturbation.change: wrap optimizer._batch_fd_gradient so it computes the gradient twice and returns the second result (cost-only regression; returned gradient, plans and objective bit-identical)
perturbation.observed_value: solver_evals ratio 1.0000 (unmoved, exact); cpu ratio 1.8071 (take 1, load1 111.24) and 1.6832 (take 2, load1 51.61), both under the 3.0 CPU concession

findings.metric_definition: sum of scipy nfev+njev over optimizer._scoped_minimize per optimizer.optimize() call

null_control.command: arm=extra_eval of tools/audit/round5/D9/work_meter_blind.py (wrap optimizer._multi_start_minimize to run twice, adding scipy evaluations)
null_control.note: the meter moves exactly 2.0000 when evaluations are added (cpu 1.91-1.94x over two takes), so it is not broken, only blind to cost-only regressions. Same load, same session.

findings.proposed_fix_scope: Add a simulate-work counter (simulate_step calls + simulate_trajectory_batch rows) to SolverWork and check it with the existing SCENARIO_WORK_FACTOR=1.5, or lower the per-scenario CPU factor from 3.0 toward the noise floor (~1.3). One file, tests/stress.py; no production change.

findings.title: DHW floor repair re-simulates the whole horizon once per weak slot (O(n^2) in horizon steps)
findings.claim: optimizer._repair_dhw_floor's inner trajectory helper simulates the full tank horizon once per weak slot; doubling the planning horizon 24h->48h multiplies its simulate_dhw_only step count by 4.02x (9408->37824) where a linear pass gives 2x, with the planner's own invocation count held constant.
findings.mechanism: After the joint raise is rejected, the per-slot loop calls trajectory(raised) (a full 96- or 192-step tank simulation) for every weak slot, plus a second trajectory(plan) whenever a slot is zeroed to refresh base. Both the weak-slot count and the steps per call scale with the horizon, so calls x steps ~ n^2. Control: _build_dhw_requirements itself is invoked the same number of times at both horizons (dhw_plan_calls=2), so a doubled planner invocation cannot explain the 4x.

evidence.machine: Apple M1 8 GB, macOS 25.6.0, numpy on OpenBLAS, threads pinned to 1

findings.instrumented_symbol: thermal_model:ThermalModel.simulate_dhw_only, attributed to optimizer:_repair_dhw_floor's inner trajectory helper (optimizer.py:5429); optimizer:_build_dhw_requirements for the invocation-count control

perturbation.observed_value: 4.02x (trajectory steps 9408->37824; planner invocations constant: dhw_plan_calls=2 both arms; total simulate_dhw_only calls 118->222); a linear re-simulation would give 2.0x

findings.metric_definition: simulate_dhw_only steps attributed to optimizer:_repair_dhw_floor's inner trajectory helper, per optimize() call

null_control.note: with the tank off the repair does not run and the count is exactly zero. The invocation-count arm is the second control: _build_dhw_requirements runs twice at BOTH horizons (dhw_plan_calls=2), so a doubled planner invocation cannot account for the 4x. Same load, same session.

findings.proposed_fix_scope: In _repair_dhw_floor's per-slot loop (optimizer.py:5451-5466), refresh only the trajectory tail from the first touched slot onward and/or re-simulate incrementally instead of trajectory(plan) after each zeroing. One function.
